headline: A traversal from one unvisited vertex reaches exactly its component
statement: Given n vertices labeled 0..n-1 and undirected edges, return the number of connected components, including isolated vertices.
constraints: Edges connect distinct valid vertices and contain no duplicates
intuition: Start from an unvisited vertex and follow every reachable edge. All vertices found belong to one connected group. Mark them so the next scan does not count that group again. Repeat from each remaining unvisited vertex, including isolated vertices with no edges.
approach: Build adjacency lists in both directions.
Scan all n vertices, skipping previously visited ones.
For a new vertex, increase components and explore its neighbors with a stack.
Mark vertices when adding them to prevent duplicate pending work.
correctness: Following undirected edges reaches all and only vertices connected to the start. Marking the traversal result prevents recounting that component. Every vertex is scanned, so even an isolated vertex starts exactly one traversal; the total starts equals the components.
bruteForce: For each vertex recompute reachability from scratch and deduplicate resulting sets: O(n*(n+e)) time.

complexity.explanation: Time O(n+e); additional space O(n+e). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: Add both directions for every undirected edge.
An isolated vertex counts as a component.
Mark on push so cycles do not enqueue the same node repeatedly.
